claims.text: KZTV, June 19th 2026: federal, state and local agencies held a drone demonstration in Jim Wells County on Friday to show technologies being considered to track, monitor and combat the New World screwworm.
claims.quote: Federal, state and local agencies held a drone demonstration in Jim Wells County on Friday, showcasing new technologies being considered to help track, monitor and combat the new world screwworm.

claims.text: The demonstration highlighted how drones, cameras and artificial intelligence could be used to identify animals that may be injured or infested in hard-to-reach areas.
claims.quote: The demonstration highlighted how drones, cameras and artificial intelligence could be used to identify animals that may be injured or infested in areas that are difficult to reach.

claims.text: Michael Schmoyer of USDA APHIS said the approach works well on feral swine and asked whether it can be used for screwworms.

claims.text: Schmoyer described the goal as taking something that works and applying it to screwworms.

claims.text: Officials say technology is one part of the plan and the sterile fly program remains the most effective weapon.
claims.quote: While technology is one part of the plan, officials say the most effective weapon against the screwworm remains the sterile fly program.

claims.text: John Bellinger, lead advisor to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins, said he treated screwworm on calves at his grandfather's place in Wilson County and that it is back.

claims.text: Bellinger said wildlife is one of the biggest challenges because white-tailed deer and feral hogs can become hosts without anyone knowing they have been injured.
claims.quote: Bellinger said wildlife poses one of the biggest challenges in combating the parasite. White-tailed deer and feral hogs can become hosts without anyone knowing they have been injured.

claims.text: Local producers have been urged to inspect their animals more often and report suspected cases.
claims.quote: Local producers have been urged to increase inspections of their animals and report any suspected cases of screwworm infestation.

claims.text: A surveillance demonstration on a South Texas ranch in Nueces County laid out alternative approaches to confront the fly.
claims.quote: At a recent surveillance demonstration on a South Texas ranch in Nueces County, government officials and field expert advisers laid out alternative approaches to confront the parasitic fly.

claims.text: Helicopters and drones will scout and locate wild animals and livestock in south and southwestern Texas, where the screwworm is flying north over the border.

claims.text: Spotters from above and on the ground will rely on cameras, infrared, night vision, heat sensors, dogs and AI to take a closer look at animals potentially infected.
